project_type: AgilIA MVP — Node/TypeScript document-intelligence + rule-engine service on bun, with a Hono local HTTP server and a static Tailwind SPA. Local-first provider abstraction over an AWS serverless target (Textract/Comprehend/Bedrock/S3/DynamoDB/OpenSearch).
build_system: bun 1.4.4 as runtime AND package manager. node is NOT installed; git is NOT installed. Use bun for everything. Type-check with `bunx tsc --noEmit` (typescript is a devDependency). No bundling needed to run; `bun run <file.ts>` executes TS directly.
test_framework: bun test (built-in, Jest-like API via `import { test, expect, describe } from "bun:test"`).
verification_instructions: 1) `bun install`. 2) `bunx tsc --noEmit` must be clean across src/ (local AND aws providers). 3) `bun test` must pass. 4) The HTTP server is verified IN-PROCESS via Hono `app.fetch(new Request(...))` inside bun test — never start a long-running listener in verification; Windows PowerShell must not be left with a blocking process. A manual demo run uses `bun run dev` (listens on PORT, default 8787) but that is NOT part of automated verification.
snapshot_or_generated_files: Local providers write runtime state under c:\Users\jparrap\AgilIA-AWS\.data\ (documents, drafts, versions). This is runtime data, not checked-in source; gitignore is moot (git absent) but keep it out of any packaging. No codegen/snapshot step.

contribution_requirements: Construction-phase guardrails: complete runnable files (no stub-that-always-passes); error handling at every I/O boundary (file, HTTP, future SDK) — no silent failures; no hardcoded secrets (use env / .env.example); validate+sanitize inputs at the HTTP boundary (zod); no PII in logs; tests must cover happy path + >=2 edge/error cases and must not use always-true asserts; flag the local server's missing auth explicitly in code and README (Cognito is the production auth boundary).
key_patterns: Provider abstraction: 7 interfaces (DocumentExtractor, NlpAnalyzer, RuleValidator, DraftGenerator, Storage, TraceStore, SearchIndex) in src/providers/interfaces.ts; a `local` bundle (fully offline, deterministic, demoable) and a `thin` `aws` bundle (compiles, wired to AWS SDK, future wiring point) selected by env AIDLC_PROVIDER=local|aws (default local) via src/providers/index.ts using a DYNAMIC import() for the aws module so local runtime never loads the SDK. Findings carry {severity, category, message(explanation), evidence(textual), location, riskAlert?}. Draft = structured sections + Markdown `content`, editable, with `[[COMPLETAR: ...]]` placeholders and finding markers. Rules are REAL business rules (see plan.md table), mirroring the inconsistencies product-final.html demonstrates (sin-IVA vs con-IVA value mismatch, closed brand 'Mac', restrictive experience).
